trigger: operator reads ADR-0040 Update/upgrading.md rollback-caution prose to decide whether rolling back an upgraded AuditStore is safe
summary: Rollback-caution prose had the mechanism backwards: claimed marker-absent+no-legacy-file is the ordinary safe/silent case, when complete_without_source's pg_rows_before>0 guard actually refuses whenever audit_events is non-empty -- true almost immediately after any real upgrade. Independently re-verified against git show 8992b5274 before accepting. Fixed by rewriting ADR-0040's Update and upgrading.md's rollback-caution section.

trigger: server boots with a real legacy audit.db present, now routed through the generic legacy_sqlite_probe helper for the first time
summary: audit_events.detail may hold a plaintext secret from a historical, now-fixed bug (pre-fix config.update rows); the new construction-site call to legacy_sqlite_probe::warn_if_legacy_rows did not first harden the legacy file to 0600, unlike WebhookStore's established precedent for the same risk class. Fixed by adding harden_legacy_file_0600 before warn_if_legacy_rows.

trigger: reader reads audit_store.cpp's constructor and seed_last_pass_from_anchor doc comments after migrate_from_sqlite was deleted
summary: Constructor and seed_last_pass_from_anchor doc comments still referenced migrate_from_sqlite/backfill_ok (both deleted) -- the .hpp twin had been corrected but the parallel .cpp comments were missed. Independently found by architect, cpp-expert, cpp-safety, sre, quality-engineer (5 agents, same cluster). Fixed by rewriting both comment blocks to match the corrected .hpp language.

trigger: operator reads upgrading.md's AuditStore section after the new harden_legacy_file_0600 call was added at the construction site
summary: upgrading.md claimed 'untouched... nothing reads or modifies it' for the legacy audit.db, self-contradicting the same doc's own 'opens it read-only' line and the actual new harden_legacy_file_0600 call, which DOES modify file permissions. Fixed by rewriting to accurately describe the 0600-hardening + read-only row-count check.

trigger: operator compares the generic legacy_sqlite_probe boot-log 'reapply manually' phrasing against AuditStore-specific 'no automated recovery path' text
summary: Tension between the shared warn_if_legacy_rows boot-log string ('reapply manually') and AuditStore-specific text ('no automated recovery path... Yuzu will never import it') -- audit trail is historical evidence, not operator-authored config you'd reapply. Fixed by adding a clarifying sentence distinguishing config-shaped stores (reapply = re-create via API) from AuditStore (reapply = export-and-archive).

trigger: an old (pre-retirement) binary boots while audit_events is still empty, the near-guaranteed window immediately after the v2 DELETE migration runs, before any native write
summary: Sticky marker re-stamp: old binary's marker-absent+empty-table branch re-stamps backfill_complete='sourceless' via Sourceless::StampIfEmpty; since v2 never re-runs, the stamp is permanent, so every LATER old-binary boot takes the marker-present branch, which returns success with zero row-count check -- one lost race permanently and silently disarms the refusal. Initial fix: CHECK constraint added in bec24602e (later found itself defective when split into v2/v3 by 273a45f4b -- see pass 4; final fix recombines into one atomic migration in ea60c923b).

trigger: the break-glass CLI (--mfa-reset/--break-glass-arm) is run from a freshly-built image against a fleet whose daemons haven't yet upgraded
summary: open_one_shot_audit constructs a full AuditStore unconditionally, able to manufacture UP-1's empty-table race window directly against a live, not-yet-upgraded fleet, outside any planned rollout. Same CHECK-constraint fix as UP-1 closes this (the CLI shares the same constructor).

trigger: reader compares upgrading.md's RbacStore-vs-AuditStore rollback comparison paragraph against RbacStore's actual v4 migration
summary: Claimed RbacStore's marker rows are 'removed, not the table... 0 rows, not a SQL error' -- false: RbacStore's v4 migration POISONS the rows in place (ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE to 'sourceless'), never deletes them. An old binary finds 2 rows present with sentinel values, not 0. Fixed by rewriting to describe the poisoned-row lookup.

trigger: reader checks ADR-0040 Update's claim that the legacy-file-present backfill path never consults pg_rows_before, against the pre-retirement source's prefix-fingerprint block
summary: Claimed the streamed-backfill path 'never consults pg_rows_before' -- false, the prefix-proof block builds pg_before{pg_rows_before,...} and refuses on mismatch. Errs toward understating the safety net (not operationally dangerous) but is a verified factual error. Fixed by correcting the parenthetical (later superseded entirely by the CHECK-constraint rewrite in ea60c923b).

trigger: reader compares postgres-migration-ladder.md's AuditStore row's 'two new counters' claim against its own later 'backfill_total also removed' sentence in the same cell
summary: Self-contradiction within one paragraph: retained 'the two new ADR-0040 counters... and backfill_total' as present-tense fact, then later in the same cell says backfill_total is removed. The parallel enterprise-readiness-soc2-first-customer.md row had already been fixed correctly (singular framing). Fixed by matching that row's pattern.

trigger: reader checks postgres-store-playbook.md line 11's ADR-0009 summary against the PR's own new text stating no store on the ladder has a migrate_from_sqlite() today
summary: Pre-existing line ('stays in place for already-migrated stores') contradicted by this PR's own new text elsewhere in the same file. Fixed by updating the ADR-0009 summary line.

trigger: reader checks the migration comment's citation of RbacStore's CHECK constraint version number against rbac_store.cpp
summary: Cited 'RbacStore's own v4 constraint' for the rbac_meta_enabled_canonical CHECK constraint -- that constraint is actually RbacStore's v2; RbacStore's real v4 is the unrelated poison-insert fix for the backfill markers. Fix in 273a45f4b introduced a NEW mixup by changing the wrong occurrence (see 3623-19, pass 5) -- the correct fix was applied in ced2c0e11.

trigger: reader checks the migration comment's claim that the CHECK constraint rejects an old binary's write 'on EVERY branch' against the four sub-cases the comment itself enumerates
summary: Only 2 of 4 old-binary rollback branches actually reach the INSERT the CHECK constraint blocks; the other 2 were already refused by a pre-existing row-count guard or are structurally unreachable post-migration, not CHECK-rejected. The end-to-end safety outcome is correct; only the claimed uniform mechanism was imprecise. Fixed by distinguishing the three actual mechanisms.

trigger: a persistent (non-recreated) Postgres instance was already migrated by an earlier build of this branch (f9c0624d3's DELETE-only v2), before this round's CHECK-constraint fix existed
summary: In-place edit of v2's SQL text risks silent drift on any persistent DB that already ran the prior commit's DELETE-only v2, since PgMigrationRunner tracks only an integer version with no content checksum. Verified clean on the two Postgres instances reachable from this box (yuzu-native-uat-postgres, yuzu-homeserver-postgres, both still v1) and via git merge-base ancestor check (branch never shipped). This SHOULD directly motivated the v2/v3 split in 273a45f4b, which chaos-injector (pass 4) then found reopened a WORSE race; the split was reverted in ea60c923b and the drift concern answered via the recorded verification instead (kept in the migration comment).

trigger: re-verification of 3623-6-UP1/UP2 against bec24602e's CHECK constraint
summary: Re-verified UP-1 and UP-2 CLOSED against bec24602e's CHECK constraint: empirically confirmed ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING does not bypass a CHECK violation (raw psql probe), traced the full pre-retirement migrate_from_sqlite body end to end, confirmed no incidental insertion path. Not a new finding -- closure confirmation of 3623-6-UP1/UP2.

trigger: process crashes between v2's COMMIT and v3's BEGIN (both now separate migrations after 273a45f4b's split); an old binary -- which does not take PgMigrationRunner's advisory lock, by its own design -- lands a marker INSERT into that gap
summary: The v2/v3 split (introduced by 273a45f4b to address 3623-13's drift concern) reopened a race WORSE than UP-1: v3's ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT then fails validating the row it finds, wedging the CURRENT (correct) binary's own boot -- not just an old binary's rollback attempt -- until an operator manually deletes the row. Fixed by recombining v2+v3 into one atomic migration (DELETE then ADD CONSTRAINT, one transaction, DELETE-first for self-healing retries) in ea60c923b.

trigger: future auditor reads ADR-0040's header line to determine whether the ADR was accepted
summary: ADR-0040 header still reads Status: Proposed despite three prior Updates plus this one -- pre-existing, not introduced by this PR, left as an accepted judgment call (not fixed this round -- out of PR scope).

trigger: reader compares ADR-0040's description of the boot-time detect path against the actual server.cpp construction site
summary: ADR-0040 described the boot-time path as 'WARN-only, log-only, never blocking' but omitted that it also runs harden_legacy_file_0600 (a permissions change) -- disclosed correctly in upgrading.md but not in the ADR named as authoritative. Fixed by mentioning harden_legacy_file_0600 alongside warn_if_legacy_rows in the ADR.

trigger: an operator running AuditStore in a multi-replica/HA topology performs a staged rollout; any replica or break-glass CLI image still on the pre-retirement binary boots after a sibling has already applied the new migration
summary: No operator-facing guidance existed for coordinating a multi-replica AuditStore rollout against the new CHECK constraint, which makes ANY old binary permanently unable to boot against a migrated database. Not novel to this PR (same gap exists for every hard-cutover-migrated store), but cheap to add. Fixed by adding a rollout-coordination sentence to upgrading.md's Rollback caution paragraph.

trigger: a Windows server operator with a legacy audit.db containing real (possibly plaintext-secret) content reads upgrading.md's/audit-log.md's 0600-hardening claim
summary: upgrading.md and audit-log.md claimed legacy audit.db permissions 'are forced to owner-only (0600)... same obligation as every other legacy-file-hardening store on this page' without disclosing that harden_legacy_file_0600 is POSIX-only and a documented no-op on Windows (#3593) -- Yuzu ships Windows server builds, and the sibling WebhookStore section on the same page correctly discloses this caveat. Fixed in ea60c923b (both files); a second uncaveated restatement 11 lines below the fixed instance in upgrading.md was found by this same reviewer's Gate 8 re-check and fixed in ced2c0e11 (see 3623-21).

trigger: an operator who deployed the pre-PR yuzu-alerts.yml upgrades without re-syncing it
summary: Removing yuzu_server_audit_backfill_total retires the YuzuAuditBackfillFailing alert; an operator on a stale local rules copy gets a CRITICAL page that never clears (absent_over_time), pointing at boot-log remediation steps that no longer exist. This exact hazard class has an established 'What to do:' convention elsewhere in the same doc that the AuditStore section didn't follow. Fixed by adding a 'What to do:' callout matching the established convention.

trigger: prospective enterprise customer's security team reads upgrading.md's AuditStore rollback-caution wording during a pre-purchase questionnaire
summary: 'the operator directed a hard cutover... accepting permanent audit-trail loss' leaks internal governance vocabulary into customer-facing text, where sibling sections use impersonal phrasing. Fixed by rewording to impersonal ('this is a hard cutover...').

trigger: re-verification of 3623-15 (scenario #2) against the recombined atomic v2 migration in ea60c923b
summary: Re-verified scenario #2 CLOSED: traced PgTxn's rollback-on-failure via pg_raii.hpp, confirmed no durable intermediate state exists (crash-before-commit collapses to 'migration never ran'), confirmed self-healing-retry semantics against PgMigrationRunner's actual failure/restart behavior, spot-checked scenario #1 (concurrent replicas) unaffected, confirmed no new hazard from combining two DDL statements in one transaction. Not a new finding -- closure confirmation of 3623-15.

trigger: reader checks the migration comment's citation of stamp_complete's marker INSERT conflict target against the pre-retirement source
summary: Comment cited stamp_complete's marker INSERT as 'ON CONFLICT (id)' -- verified against git show 8992b5274 that the marker insert actually targets ON CONFLICT (key) (audit_retention_meta's PK is key; (id) is correct only for the unrelated audit_events row-copy insert). Carried over unchanged from 273a45f4b, pre-existing to this specific commit. Doesn't affect the security conclusion (CHECK validates before conflict arbitration regardless of target column). Fixed in ced2c0e11.

trigger: future migration author needs to encode 'these two DDL/DML statements must be atomic' and looks for a named rule in the playbook
summary: postgres-store-playbook.md has no rule for 'when must two statements share one migration entry', only worked examples now (RbacStore v4, AuditStore v2). Not fixed this round -- deferred as a documentation follow-up, not blocking this PR.

trigger: reader compares audit_store.cpp's/ADR-0040's 'RbacStore's v2' poison-migration citation against rbac_store.cpp and ADR-0041
summary: The prior round's fix for 3623-11 (architect's v4-vs-v2 NICE) corrected the WRONG occurrence: 'the opposite choice from RbacStore's v2' should say v4 (the poison-marker migration); the CORRECT v2 reference (for the CHECK-constraint shape) was two paragraphs later and already right. Root cause was in the code comment from 273a45f4b, propagated into ADR-0040 by ea60c923b's own edit. Independently found by docs-writer and enterprise-readiness (both flagged the RbacStore-numbering confusion, though enterprise-readiness's own report focused on the separate 0600 restatement, 3623-26). Fixed in ced2c0e11: both v2 occurrences corrected to v4 (audit_store.cpp:216, ADR-0040:355).

trigger: a Windows operator reads only upgrading.md's second 0600 restatement (11 lines below the fixed first instance) in isolation
summary: upgrading.md's AuditStore section restates the 0600-hardening claim a second time ('0600 now enforced, content otherwise untouched') without the POSIX-only/Windows-no-op caveat just added 11 lines above -- the same false-assurance gap 3623-19 was fixed to remove, reopened in a second location within the same commit that fixed the first. Independently found by docs-writer and enterprise-readiness (3623-27, same underlying defect, two independent reports). Fixed in ced2c0e11 by adding '(0600 now enforced on POSIX, #3593; ...)'.

trigger: same trigger as 3623-26 -- a Windows operator reads upgrading.md's second, uncaveated 0600 restatement
summary: Re-verification of 3623-19 found it REOPENED in a smaller form: the primary site (line 1774) now correctly carries the caveat, but a second restatement 8-11 lines below (line 1785) does not. Duplicate finding of 3623-26 (docs-writer independently found the same defect). Fixed together in ced2c0e11.
